subject: Archaeology
title: The Spanish Armada Wrecks
description: A quick, practical guide to The Spanish Armada Wrecks.

hook.text: In 1588, Spain sent 130 ships to invade England. Storms wrecked dozens along the coasts of Ireland and Scotland.

buildup.text: The English fleet used fire ships and long-range cannons to scatter the Armada into the North Sea.

discovery.text: Divers have found cannons, anchors, gold coins, and personal items from Armada wrecks off the Irish coast.

twist.text: Many sailors who survived the wrecks were killed by locals on shore.

climax.text: The Girona wreck off Northern Ireland yielded a gold salamander pendant and a ruby ring — personal treasures of Spanish nobles.

punchline.text: Spain sent 130 ships. The sea returned jewelry, cannons.

quiz.question: What happened to many Spanish Armada sailors who survived the wrecks?
options: They were welcomed and settled permanently in Ireland
They were killed by locals since Ireland was English territory
They were captured and ransomed back to Spain

details.summary: When the Spanish Armada was scattered by English fireships and storms in 1588, dozens of ships wrecked along the coasts of Ireland and Scotland. Underwater excavations of these wrecks have recovered cannon, personal items, and navigation equipment that reveal the human reality behind this legendary.
details.whyItMatters: Armada wrecks provide physical evidence to test and correct historical narratives written by the victors. Artifacts reveal the crew's daily life, health, and equipment in ways that English propaganda and Spanish official reports both distort.
takeaways: Dozens of Armada ships wrecked along Irish and Scottish coasts
Excavations recovered cannon, personal items, and instruments
Artifacts correct biased historical narratives from both sides

faq.question: How many Armada ships were lost?
faq.answer: Of the original 130 ships, approximately 35-45 were lost. Most sank in storms while attempting to return to Spain by sailing around Scotland and Ireland. Crews who reached shore in Ireland were often killed by English forces or local authorities loyal to the English crown.

faq.question: What have Armada wrecks revealed?
faq.answer: The Girona wreck off Northern Ireland yielded gold jewelry, coins, and personal items revealing the wealth and status of Spanish officers. Other wrecks show that many ships carried outdated cannon and deteriorating supplies, contributing to the Armada's tactical disadvantage.
